content.title: Year in Review
content.summary: In 2025, Arvada's Infrastructure Department made significant advancements in maintaining and modernizing the city's critical systems, including upgrading over 85 traffic signals to enhance travel efficiency and safety. Key achievements included repaving 147 lane miles, replacing more than 260 sidewalk ramps for ADA accessibility, and responding to 12 snowstorms by plowing over 35,000 miles of road. The department's efforts aim to create a reliable, resilient infrastructure that supports the community's needs year-round.
content.body:
## 2025 Infrastructure services: A year in review

Reliable infrastructure is at the foundation of what makes Arvada a thriving community. The Infrastructure Department plans, builds, operates, and maintains the critical systems and structures that sustain our community. Behind each number—every pothole filled, every bike lane added, every storm or sewer pipe cleaned, and every drop of water delivered to your tap—there is a story. This is a snapshot of the work of our dedicated professionals in 2025.

### Featured story: Smart signals, smoother travel

Nate Sexton, the City’s Traffic Operations and Maintenance Manager, has been leading the effort to modernize traffic signal infrastructure, upgrading controllers, detections systems, and cameras to improve reliability. By connecting signals to the City’s fiber network, the City can maintain precise timing, identify and resolve issues remotely, improve coordination during incidents, and prepare for future adaptive and connected vehicle technologies.

![man in utility vest reaching into utility box outside with lots of wires and equipment](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6683)

> "Coordinated signals reduce unnecessary stops, congestion, and emissions while ensuring faster response to outages or detection issues. These improvements create safer intersections and more predictable travel times."
>
> **— Nate Sexton**, Traffic Operations and Maintenance Manager

Today, Nate and the traffic team have **upgraded more than 85 of the 100+ signals**in Arvada. This year alone, 31 signals received upgraded detection systems, one signal was rebuilt, and one new signal was installed. This effort supports the City’s long-term goals of building a reliable, resilient, and smart traffic system, making Arvada a leader in municipal traffic signal modernization.

### Featured story: 24/7 response for reliable water 365

At 9:00 pm on a Wednesday, Utilities Technician Xavian answers the City’s after-hours phone to a resident reporting water coming out of the street. On site, Xavian assesses the incident and a team of 4 others, Mike, Colton, Cooper, and Angelo, are called in to help repair a water main break. The team arrived with excavation equipment, coordinated with utility locators, and got to work. They safely dug down to the damaged pipe and applied a repair clamp to stop the leak within just a few hours. Twelve households were affected by the break, but the team was able to maintain water pressure and keep contaminants out of the pipe to maintain service throughout the repair.

![two people in construction gear working with large utility equipment next to a whole in the ground](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6685)

> "Water main breaks happen, but thanks to the professionals we have in house, we always have a strong crew ready to react and deliver excellent service. Our construction crew is a very strong unit, and we have a great training program to get our entire division ready for these after-hour incidents."
>
> **— Mike Morris**, Water Utility Foreman

Every break can be different, in this case many of the conditions for the repair were favorable. Sometimes customers experience a drop in water pressure or need to have their water turned off. Additionally, underground utility conflicts or ground material can cause the repair to take up to 8 hours. Our teams are ready to respond and maintain high-quality, reliable drinking water service, rain or shine, 24/7, 365.

## APWA AccreditedAPWA accreditation logo

The City of Arvada achieved its 2nd [re-accreditation with the](https://www.apwa.org/resources/accreditation/)[American Public Works Association (APWA)](https://www.apwa.org/) in 2023. The evaluation and best practice review process provides a means of formally verifying and recognizing public works agencies for compliance with the recommended practices. The City of Arvada was first accredited in 2016 with re-accreditations in 2020 and 2023.
